# Brand: KC Santana

## Identity

KC Santana is the mentor for high-earning, undisciplined women who shows them by living it that fitness discipline is the answer. No shortcuts. No GLP-1s. No excuses.

Cannabis sits inside that life as a tool she uses, not a flag she waves. The special needs mother layer is unspoken fuel: the reason she cannot afford to skip a day, not a story she sells.

KC is a founder-led personal brand at Founder Spectrum position 5. The founder is the proof. The brand must show her standard, her discipline, her presence, and her refusal of shortcuts without turning her into a coach, wellness influencer, stoner personality, or soft nurturing lifestyle figure.

## Focus Star

### Center: No Excuses

No Excuses is the operating contract. It is not motivational filler. It means the brand refuses shortcuts, passive health, GLP-1-as-identity, lazy stoner stereotypes, and pretty wellness language that does not change behavior.

Every event, post, podcast, future product, speaking moment, and visual direction should answer the same question: does this make discipline feel inevitable?

### P1 Product: Thought leadership with proof

**Decision:** KC's current product is proof-led thought leadership delivered through wellness events, mastermind dinners, podcasting, content, and emerging speaking. She is a mentor and thought leader, not a coach and not an educator.

**Compass:** Follow the woman who lives the standard. Events, podcast, content, and speaking all point to one discipline-first life.

**Page thesis:** The product is not a program yet. The product is KC's visible standard: a daily proof system that makes high-earning women stop outsourcing discipline.

**Rules in:**
- Wellness events and mastermind dinners anchored in SoCal.
- Intimate rooms of women who need the standard more than another self-care idea.
- Podcast and content that make discipline visible.
- Speaking as the natural extension of mentor and thought-leader authority.
- Cannabis as one functional tool in the discipline stack.
- Future products named only as future products.

**Rules out:**
- Coaching package positioning.
- Educator-first positioning.
- Generic wellness content.
- Cannabis SKU as the current center.
- GLP-1 or shortcut framing.
- Passive lifestyle inspiration.

**Tradeoffs:**
- More authority through lived proof, less scalable coaching language.
- More demand on KC's visibility, less ability to hide behind a curriculum.
- More directness and standard-setting, less comfort-first nurturing.

**Application:**
- **Strategy:** lead with thought leadership and lived proof before naming future products.
- **Copy:** use command, standard, and proof language. Do not over-explain.
- **Visuals:** show strength, discipline, event authority, and performance ritual.
- **Sales:** invite women into rooms and conversations that raise the standard.
- **Content:** make daily discipline, training, functional cannabis, and no-shortcut beliefs visible.

**Proof required:**
- Source line: wellness events are the way KC makes an impact and holds authority.
- Source line: role is mentor / thought leader, not coach or educator.
- Existing podcast proof.
- Event history, event photos, or event plans if available.
- Speaking proof when available.

**AI instructions:**
- Do not sell a coaching program unless source changes.
- Do not invent event outcomes, audience size, podcast metrics, or product claims.
- Keep future products clearly marked as future.
- Position cannabis as part of the discipline stack, not the offer itself.

**Image:** Direction board pending in Section B.

### P2 People: High-earning women who need the standard

**Decision:** KC serves high-earning, health-curious, undisciplined women in SoCal who know something has to change but do not know where to start. The primary persona is Alina.

**Compass:** Alina: 35, SoCal, good salary, health-conscious but undisciplined, holistic-leaning, and awkward around cannabis.

**Page thesis:** KC is not speaking to women who need more information. She is speaking to women who need a standard they cannot negotiate with.

**Rules in:**
- High-earning SoCal women.
- Corporate, banking, Cedars-Sinai-nurse, and similar high-functioning archetypes.
- Women who are health-curious and holistic-leaning.
- Women who consume cannabis awkwardly or without a disciplined frame.
- Special-needs moms as an identity layer, not the primary segment.
- One bio line for mother of three when relevant.

**Rules out:**
- Lazy stoner stereotypes.
- GLP-1 or shortcut seekers.
- Pink-Barbie feminine wellness.
- Infantilized mom content.
- Public use of her son's face.
- Treating special-needs moms as the front of the brand.

**Tradeoffs:**
- More precision around Alina, less broad wellness appeal.
- More standard-setting, less soothing.
- More adult feminine power, less cute community language.

**Application:**
- **Strategy:** speak to women who can afford wellness but have not built discipline.
- **Copy:** name the behavior gap without humiliating the woman.
- **Visuals:** show capable, high-standard women in fitness, dinner, and performance spaces.
- **Sales:** make the room feel selective through behavior, not status snobbery.
- **Content:** connect discipline to cognitive longevity, hormonal health, physical health, and daily proof.

**Proof required:**
- Persona notes for Alina.
- Geographic note: SoCal, not Inland Empire and not LA-only.
- Source statement that special-needs moms are an identity layer only.
- Approved bio direction before public use.

**AI instructions:**
- Keep Alina capable. The issue is undisciplined health behavior, not incompetence.
- Do not make the brand mommy-first.
- Do not use her son's image or turn special needs motherhood into a selling story.
- Avoid pink, princess, cutesy, or therapy-soft femininity.

**Image:** Direction board pending in Section B.

### P3 Purpose: Women's health through discipline

**Decision:** KC exists to help women reclaim cognitive longevity, hormonal health, physical health, and mental health through lifestyle discipline, weighted heavily toward fitness and discipline.

**Compass:** The point is not to change every woman. The point is to make the better way visible enough that excuses get harder to defend.

**Page thesis:** KC's purpose is personal before it is public: she watched women close to her ignore the advice and arrive at diagnoses that might have been delayed or avoided. Her authority comes from living the standard herself: as a special-needs mother, she has to treat strength, longevity, and discipline as non-optional.

**Rules in:**
- Cognitive longevity.
- Hormonal and physical health.
- Mental health as part of the discipline frame.
- Fitness and lifestyle discipline as the dominant levers.
- Close-to-home health wake-up calls, used carefully and without medical overclaiming.
- Special-needs motherhood as the lived stake behind the standard, not the public selling story.
- Awareness that there is a better way.

**Rules out:**
- Medical claims.
- Diagnosis prevention claims.
- Weight-loss-before-after framing.
- Soft wellness inspiration without discipline.
- Fear tactics without behavior.
- Clinical therapy or pharma imagery.

**Tradeoffs:**
- More direct health urgency, higher need for evidence discipline.
- More anti-shortcut conviction, less appeal to women seeking easy solutions.
- More personal stakes, less public oversharing.

**Application:**
- **Strategy:** make discipline the health intervention the brand can credibly own because KC lives the long-haul stakes herself.
- **Copy:** connect health to behavior, not hacks.
- **Visuals:** show training, recovery, routine, daylight, and controlled intensity.
- **Sales:** frame events as authority-building rooms around standards and practice.
- **Content:** make prevention language careful and source-backed.

**Proof required:**
- KC source quote: "If I can do it, anybody else can. No more excuses."
- KC source quote about making women aware there is a better way.
- Any future medical, longevity, or hormonal-health claims need source evidence.

**AI instructions:**
- Do not make medical promises.
- Do not claim KC prevents disease.
- Do not use GLP-1 imagery, scales, before-after bodies, white coats, or pill bottles.
- Keep the purpose practical and behavioral.

**Image:** Direction board pending in Section B.

### P4 Promise: No Excuses

**Decision:** The brand promise is No Excuses. KC will not sell the shortcut. She will be the voice that makes Alina do the work.

**Compass:** No shortcuts. No GLP-1 identity. No passive wellness. No excuses.

**Page thesis:** No Excuses is a refusal and an invitation. It says the body, the brain, the hormones, the training, the work, and the room all answer to the same standard.

**Rules in:**
- Primary tagline: No Excuses.
- Alternate lines: Earn it. Effort is the answer. Discipline doesn't lie. Show up. No exceptions.
- Anti-GLP-1 and anti-shortcut as bright-line proof.
- Anti-passive health.
- Tough-love mentor voice.

**Rules out:**
- Weight-loss promises.
- Shaming bodies.
- Generic hustle slogans.
- Cute motivational posters.
- Wellness-guru calm.
- Any language that makes discipline sound optional.

**Tradeoffs:**
- More edge and conviction, less broad comfort.
- More clear rejection of shortcuts, higher need not to shame bodies or medical choices.
- More memorable promise, less room for soft brand ambiguity.

**Application:**
- **Strategy:** use No Excuses as the decision filter across products, content, events, and visuals.
- **Copy:** short sentences, direct commands, hard contrast.
- **Visuals:** geometric structure, discipline marks, training evidence, serious contrast.
- **Sales:** make event participation feel like stepping into the standard.
- **Content:** make the refusal visible without turning it into cruelty.

**Proof required:**
- KC source quote about refusing fat-loss drugs and putting in the work.
- Approved tagline list.
- Approved anti-persona list.

**AI instructions:**
- Do not soften No Excuses into generic empowerment.
- Do not moralize medical choices beyond the approved anti-shortcut position.
- Do not use body-shaming imagery or copy.
- Keep the promise pointed at behavior and standards.

**Image:** Direction board pending in Section B.

### P5 Personality: Disciplined badassness

**Decision:** KC's personality is disciplined badassness: Hero and Ruler tied for primary, Magician as transformation, and Cannabis Outlaw as the category edge. She is the special-needs mom of three, corporate woman, and cannabis wellness voice who still gives 100% when excuses would be understandable.

**Compass:** Badass willpower in a SoCal mom's voice: corporate-trained, cannabis-literate, mother of three, and still all-in.

**Page thesis:** KC's difference is not that she talks about cannabis, fitness, motherhood, or corporate grit. It is that every layer proves the same thing: she has the willpower to do the work anyway.

**Rules in:**
- Badass discipline, willpower, and 100% effort when excuses would be understandable.
- Authoritative, bold, brave, determined, disruptive, empowering, fearless, honest.
- Inspiring, knowledgeable, loyal, powerful, resilient, transformative, unconventional.
- Serious, literal, geometric, rational, transparent.
- Feminine through form, strength, command, and presence.
- Healthy functional fitness cannabis: sun-grown, athlete-grade, pre-workout or post-recovery ritual.

**Rules out:**
- Cheeky, enchanting, entertaining, magical.
- Pink-Barbie feminine.
- Stoner, party, couch-potato, tie-dye, peace-sign, munchies, basement lighting.
- Pharma-glossy wellness.
- Therapy-soft femininity.
- Abstract, emotional, playful, mysterious, organic as dominant signals.

**Tradeoffs:**
- More commanding presence, less easy likeability.
- More rational and literal direction, less dreamy wellness imagery.
- More cannabis edge, higher need to avoid stoner and medical-victim tropes.

**Application:**
- **Strategy:** use cannabis to separate the category, not to lead the whole brand.
- **Copy:** plainspoken, unsentimental, no fluff.
- **Visuals:** geometry, hard contrast, real body discipline, event authority, controlled luxury.
- **Sales:** make the room feel high-standard, not cute or mystical.
- **Content:** let KC be the example before she becomes the explainer.

**Proof required:**
- Approved archetype mix.
- Locked attribute list.
- Slider source and anti-trope source.
- Any likeness-based image use needs explicit reference review and approval.

**AI instructions:**
- Never make KC cute, mystical, soft, or stoner-coded.
- Keep cannabis functional and athletic.
- Express femininity through strength, form, body presence, and command.
- Avoid generic wellness, generic gym, and generic cannabis imagery.

**Image:** Direction board pending in Section B.

# Brand Identity: KC Santana

## 1. Visual Theme & Atmosphere

**Core concept:** Run the Standard. KC's world is disciplined outdoor SoCal performance: training in daylight, recovery as ritual, and a functional stack where sun-grown cannabis sits next to magnesium and water. The brand shows the standard being lived, not talked about.

**Atmosphere:** sunlit, athletic, functional, controlled, alive. Hard light, real sweat, rational overlays, equipment-grade labeling. Luxury comes through control and quality, not ornament.

**Strategic temperature:** serious, literal, rational, geometric, transparent. Energy is high but governed. If a surface starts feeling calm-spa or sunny-soft, add athletic tension, data, and discipline language until it holds.

**What this brand is NOT visually:**
- Stoner lifestyle or couch cannabis.
- Beach influencer or golden-hour lifestyle softness.
- Spa wellness, pastel therapy, or pharma gloss.
- Pink Barbie empowerment.
- GLP-1 shortcut imagery, scales, before-after bodies.
- Mommy-blogger softness.

## 2. Color Palette & Roles

- **Sun Bone `#F1E2C7`:** the daylight field. Default canvas for pages, posts, and print. It is outdoor light as a surface.
- **Trail Black `#1B1712`:** type and authority. Headlines, navigation, frames, and the hard edge of every layout.
- **Performance Green `#4E6B46`:** functional cannabis and recovery. The accent that marks the stack, the ritual, and the brand's category edge. Links and focus states on Brand OS surfaces.
- **Heat Clay `#B55336`:** effort and SoCal terrain. Intensity moments, effort markers, trail heat. Used sparingly.
- **Water Steel `#405C73`:** rational overlays and recovery cues. Data strips, measurement marks, schedules, cool-down surfaces.

Derived neutrals (muted text `#6F6354`, border lines `#DCC9A4`, deep bone panels `#E8D5AE`) stay inside the warm bone-and-earth world. No cool grays outside Water Steel moments.

## 3. Typography Rules

- **Display: Barlow Condensed.** Headlines, command lines, standards, event titles. Condensed, athletic, utilitarian. Weight 700-800 for commands, 500-600 for supporting display.
- **Body: Barlow.** Plainspoken rational body text. Same superfamily as the display face: one disciplined system, no decorative second voice.
- **Data: IBM Plex Mono.** Performance data strips, training labels, ingredient stacks, dosage-style annotations, timestamps. This is the equipment-label voice that keeps the system rational.
- **No script fonts, no serif warmth, no rounded friendly faces.** Type never gets cute.

## 4. Component Stylings

- **Performance data strips:** thin horizontal bands in Water Steel or Trail Black carrying mono-type metrics: distance, load, time, recovery, dose. Used as section dividers and image captions.
- **Training labels:** small mono or condensed uppercase labels with hard borders, placed like gear tags on images and cards.
- **Ingredient-stack layouts:** vertical stacked lists that present the discipline stack (training, water, magnesium, mushrooms, sun-grown cannabis, sleep) like a supplement panel: measured, ordered, labeled.
- **Statement blocks:** Trail Black panels with Sun Bone condensed type for No Excuses command moments.
- **Sharp photo crops:** images cropped to the grid with hard edges, often with a data strip or label overlapping the crop line.

## 5. Layout Principles

- Grid-first, geometric, literal. Every element sits on a visible order.
- Daylight whitespace: Sun Bone breathing room instead of dense darkness; black is structure, not atmosphere.
- Rational overlays earn their place: data strips and labels annotate real content, they are never decorative texture.
- One command per surface. Layouts make a single standard impossible to miss before anything else speaks.
- Energy through diagonal photo motion and hard contrast, never through clutter or effects.

## 6. Do's and Don'ts

**Do:**
- Show training, recovery, and the functional stack in real SoCal daylight.
- Treat cannabis like equipment: measured, labeled, controlled.
- Use command language and proof: schedules, receipts, visible routine.
- Keep femininity strong: form, presence, capability.
- Weave the special-needs-mom layer through lifestyle content as lived proof.
- Keep surfaces warm-bone, sharp-edged, and rationally annotated.

**Don't:**
- No weed leaves as a primary mark, no smoke glamour, no 420 cues.
- No beach-influencer softness, no spa wellness, no pastel therapy.
- No pink Barbie, no cutesy empowerment, no sparkle.
- No GLP-1 or weight-loss shortcut imagery, no scales, no before-after bodies.
- No medical clinic language, no white coats, no pill bottles.
- No sobby special-needs-mom lead stories, and never her son's face.

## Photography Rules

**Image modes:**
- **KC as the standard:** strong, present, unsentimental, camera-aware but never influencer-cute. She is the proof, photographed like an athlete, not a host.
- **Performance ritual:** outdoor SoCal training: track, hills, trails, weights, sweat, water, grip, hard daylight.
- **Recovery ritual:** the controlled stack: recovery table, magnesium, mushrooms, sun-grown cannabis as a measured object, stretching, breath.
- **High-standard room:** wellness events, mastermind dinners, speaking and podcast tables: serious women, serious conversation, KC at the head of the room.
- **Evidence surfaces:** checklists, schedules, weights, labeled jars, water, hard shadows: the receipts of discipline.

**Treatment:** hard light, true color, sharp focus, honest sweat. Crops are tight and geometric. Overlays come from the data-strip system, not from filters.

**Forbidden imagery:** weed leaves as the main mark, smoke clouds, joints as personality, tie-dye, peace signs, munchies; pill bottles, white coats, clinical pharmacy; scales, before-after bodies, miracle weight-loss cues; hearts, sparkles, princess pastels, glitter; soft pastel therapy wellness; her son's face.

## Anti-references

- **Stoner lifestyle brand.** Couch, smoke, munchies, basement light. KC's cannabis is sun-grown, measured, and athletic. The aesthetic of laziness is the opposite of the promise.
- **Beach influencer.** Golden-hour softness, bikini-lifestyle ease, effortless living. KC's SoCal is terrain and training, not vibes.
- **Spa wellness retreat.** Calm, candles, eucalyptus, whispered self-care. This brand demands effort; it does not soothe people out of it.
- **Pharma-glossy wellness.** Clinical white, pill-bottle promises, medicalized shortcuts. KC sells behavior, not prescriptions.
- **Pink empowerment brand.** Barbie pink, glitter, yass-queen energy. Femininity here is strength and command, not cuteness.
- **GLP-1 era marketing.** Shortcut bodies, before-after panels, effortless transformation. The entire brand exists to refuse this.

## Voice

Voice is part of identity. The strategic decision about Personality lives in `STRATEGY.md`; the operational voice rules live here.

### Principles

- Rough-edged. Plainspoken. Unsentimental.
- Tough-love and demanding, not nurturing.
- Serious before playful. Rational before emotional. Transparent before mysterious. Literal before abstract.
- Commanding without body shame. The target is behavior, never bodies.
- Feminine through strength and presence, not cuteness.
- Cannabis as discipline-stack tool, not a flag.

### No-excuse language system

KC is the product. Authority comes from thought leadership and example-setting, never from coaching packages or curriculum language. "Run the standard" means show up and do it: the copy shows KC doing the work and lets the example issue the command.

- Lead with proof: the run happened, the stack is measured, the schedule is visible.
- Short sentences. Direct commands. Hard contrast.
- Refuse shortcuts by name when needed (GLP-1s, hacks, passive wellness), without moralizing at individual people.
- Never soften the standard into generic empowerment or motivational poster language.

### Special-needs-mom intertwine rule

From the 2026-06-10 session: the special-needs-mom layer is woven organically through fitness and healthy-lifestyle content. It is lived context that raises the standard, never the story being sold.

- Correct: training framed as "free therapy for a special needs mom." Correct: bringing the kids to the marathon instead of skipping it.
- It appears mid-content, as one thread of proof among many. It NEVER leads a piece, never becomes a sobby opening, and never asks for sympathy.
- Her son's face is never used. The brand never becomes mommy-first.

### On-voice examples

- "No shortcuts. Do the work."
- "The routine is not cute. That is why it works."
- "Cannabis belongs in the discipline stack, not on a basement couch."
- "If the body keeps receipts, stop acting surprised by the bill."
- "Show up. No exceptions."
- "Saturday long run. Free therapy for a special needs mom."
- "Race day. The kids came with me."

### Off-voice examples

- "Yass queen, time to glow."
- "Your wellness journey starts with self-love."
- "Cannabis vibes for your soft era."
- "Unlock your best self with effortless transformation."
- "As a special needs mom, some days I just want to cry. Here's my story."

### Banned characters

- em-dash
- en-dash

Plain hyphen-minus is fine.

### Banned phrases and tropes

- Yass queen.
- Soft era.
- Weed girl.
- Mommy wellness.
- Namaste.
- Shortcut body.
- Miracle weight loss.
- Stoner chic.
- Cannabis goddess.

## Universal AI guardrails (shared/references/llm-rules.md)

# Universal AI Guardrails

These rules apply to every brand in this workspace. `build.py` concatenates this file into every brand's `output/ai-context.md` at the end of the compile, so any AI agent loading a brand's context inherits these rules.

Brand-specific AI instructions (in each brand's `STRATEGY.md` per-P `AI instructions:` labels) take precedence when they conflict. When they don't conflict, both apply.

## Punctuation

- **No em-dashes (—) and no en-dashes (–).** Use ellipsis (...), colon, comma, or new sentence where an em-dash would go. Plain hyphen-minus (-) is fine in compound words and ranges.
- **Ellipses freely** for rhythm, irony, breathing room. Three dots, no space before, one space after. Never four dots.
- **No emojis in brand content** unless a brand's STRATEGY.md explicitly allows them.

## Honesty

- **No fabrication.** Do not invent client names, outcomes, metrics, testimonials, or empirical claims. If asked to write something that requires evidence and no evidence is in the brand source, write honestly about the gap instead of confabulating.
- **No invented stats.** Phrases like "73% of founders..." or "studies show..." are forbidden unless the specific stat is documented in the brand source with a citation.
- **No fabricated attributions.** Do not put words in named people's mouths. Quote testimonials only if they appear verbatim in the brand source.

## Openers and connectives

- **No hollow affirmations.** Forbidden openers include: "Great question!", "Certainly!", "I'd be happy to help with that.", "What a thoughtful prompt."
- **No formal essay connectives.** Forbidden: "however,", "as a result,", "in conclusion,", "it's worth noting,", "moreover,", "furthermore,", "consequently,".
- **No throat-clearing preambles.** Forbidden: "In today's landscape...", "In an increasingly complex world...", "Now more than ever..."

## Methodology vs company

- Methodology names are not company names. Refer to processes by their methodology name without personifying them as companies. Example: "the Brand Therapy process" not "at Brand Therapy" or "the Brand Therapy team".
- This applies to any brand whose offer is a methodology rather than a productized service.

## Voice posture

- **Direct observation over encouragement.** Name what's happening before suggesting what should happen.
- **Questions over assertions** where the brand voice permits. Let the reader answer instead of forcing a nod.
- **Perspective shifts over lessons.** End paragraphs and posts on a shift in how the reader sees something, not on a takeaway or moral.

## When in doubt

- **Honest admissions.** When a brand-specific rule and a universal rule conflict, the brand-specific rule wins. Document the conflict in your response so it can be reviewed.
- **Ask for evidence before claiming.** If a piece of copy makes a factual claim the brand source doesn't support, write the version without the claim. Do not invent a claim to fill the space.

## Approval discipline

- Outputs labeled "approved" must hash to the `bundle_hash` in the brand's `brand.lock.json`. If the agent detects drift between `brand.lock.json` and the current source files, halt and surface the discrepancy. Do not produce "approved-brand" content from unverified source.
- AI suggestions for changes to a brand's STRATEGY.md or IDENTITY.md go in `working-folder/{brand}-suggested-changes.md`, never directly into `brands/{slug}/`. Florian merges manually after review.

## Anti-patterns (shared/references/anti-patterns.md)

# Anti-Patterns

What AI must never do when producing content, copy, or design for any brand in this workspace. Use this as a checklist during review.

## Copy anti-patterns

- **Hollow affirmations.** "You've got this!", "Show up daily!", "Trust the process." These read as motivational filler.
- **Hustle-culture copy.** "Stop overthinking and start doing." "The journey of a thousand miles..." "Crush it."
- **First-chair founder bios.** "Meet [Founder Name]." "In their own words." "A letter from me to you." Unless a brand's spectrum is explicitly 5 (founder IS the brand) AND the brand source explicitly permits first-chair framing, default to host/messenger framing.
- **Trend-report essay voice.** "As AI democratizes X, founders must Y." "In an increasingly Z world..." Abstract, defensive, devoid of specificity.
- **Generic listicle openers.** "In this article, we'll explore 5 strategies..." "Here are 7 things every founder should know."
- **Joke-only lines.** A joke without a strategic point is decoration. If the line works without the brand thesis, cut the line.
- **Fabricated empirical generalizations.** "Most founders...", "Every CEO knows...", "Studies show...", "Research indicates..." unless the specific claim is documented in brand source.
- **Brand-as-company personification** when the brand is a methodology. "At Brand Therapy, we..." treats the methodology as an organization.

## Voice anti-patterns

- **Em-dashes (—) and en-dashes (–).** Banned across all brands. Use ellipsis, colon, comma, or period.
- **Formal connectives.** "However,", "As a result,", "Moreover,", "Furthermore,", "Consequently,", "It's worth noting,".
- **Coaching-speak.** "Unlock your potential.", "Reach the next level.", "Level up.", "10x your X.".
- **AI-generated thought-leadership voice.** Hedging-heavy, qualifier-stacked, opinion-less sentences. Compare: "It is widely understood that brand strategy plays a critical role in..." vs the direct alternative.

## AI safety anti-patterns

- **Embedded AI instructions in brand source.** Do not write `Ignore previous instructions.`, `System:`, `Assistant:`, or other model-directive language inside any brand source file (STRATEGY.md, IDENTITY.md, voice-exemplars.md, references). These create prompt injection vectors when the source is concatenated into ai-context.md. The build validator flags these patterns.
- **AI-generated content treated as approved.** AI suggestions for brand changes do not become approved source by being written. They land in `working-folder/{brand}-suggested-changes.md` and only enter `brands/{slug}/` after Florian merges manually.
- **Silent fabrication.** Filling gaps with invented stats, named clients, or empirical claims to make output feel more complete. Better to leave the gap visible.

## Design anti-patterns

These apply unless a brand's IDENTITY.md explicitly opts in to a forbidden treatment:

- Rounded pill buttons by default
- Multiple accent colors
- Glassmorphism / blurred glass panels as a primary visual concept
- Prism / crystal / 3D refraction imagery
- Selective-color B&W reveals as a brand signature
- Polaroid photo treatments
- Generic stock photography
- Avatar-size photography in editorial contexts
- Decorative motion for decoration's sake
- Dark canvas as default unless a brand explicitly chooses dark-first

## Brand-source anti-patterns

- **Strategy copy living in HTML.** Section A pages (and any rendered output) are generated from STRATEGY.md + IDENTITY.md. Do not edit rendered HTML to change strategy — it gets overwritten on the next build, and the source remains wrong.
- **Mixing approval states.** A brand's STRATEGY.md is either in a state where `brand.lock.json` validates or it is in a draft state. The `approval_status: approved` frontmatter is informational only; the real gate is `bundle_hash`.
- **Cross-brand drift.** Universal rules (this file, `llm-rules.md`) apply to every brand. A brand-specific override in STRATEGY.md is fine when explicit. Silent drift between brands is not.

## Likeness references (image generation)

Person: KC Santana

KC has a long narrow oval face with a high forehead, prominent high cheekbones over lean cheeks, a defined narrow jawline and a softly pointed chin. Slim nose, almond shaped deep brown eyes, thick dark arched brows with heavy dark eyeliner. Wide bright smile with prominent straight upper teeth. Warm olive tan skin. Very long center parted dark brown hair with caramel blonde balayage in loose waves.

To generate an image of this person with any image model: attach the face-anchor reference image (and the matching outfit turnaround when the scene needs a specific outfit), start the prompt with the likeness preamble below, then describe the scene. Check the generated face against the anchor before using the result.

Likeness preamble:

```
The attached images are reference photos of the real woman KC Santana. Generate the requested scene with this exact woman. Copy her facial identity precisely from the references: face shape, eyes, brows, eyeliner, nose, lips, smile, skin tone, and her very long dark brown hair with caramel blonde balayage. Do not invent a different woman and do not beautify, slim, or otherwise change her features.
```

Reference files:

- face-anchor: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/images/likeness/face-sheet.png (Canonical face identity sheet: eight studies of the same woman covering front, three quarter, profile, smile, and ponytail views.)
- turnaround: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/images/likeness/turnaround-training.png (Training set)
- turnaround: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/images/likeness/turnaround-trail.png (Trail run)
- turnaround: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/images/likeness/turnaround-lifting.png (Lifting)
- turnaround: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/images/likeness/turnaround-street.png (Street)
- manifest: https://brandtherapy.florianp.com/kc-santana/likeness.json

Usage rules:

- Always attach the face sheet as a reference image before generating. Text descriptions alone drift.
- Add the matching outfit turnaround as a second reference when the scene needs a specific outfit or a full body pose.
- Check the generated face against the face sheet before using the result. A rounder or fuller face than the sheet is a fail.
- Likeness references are for KC Santana brand work. Identity rules from this Brand OS still govern styling, color, and context.
